articles.title: Our favorite non-toxic pan is on sale (and five other Pfas-free kitchen deals)
articles.summary: The best non-stick pan we’ve reviewed is on sale this week, along with some other great non-toxic kitchen deals we have tested and recommend. Welcome to Worth it, where Filter editors spotlight one genuinely good discount on something we have tested and loved.
body: At the Filter, we’re on a mission to reduce microplastics and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (Pfas) in our kitchens. It is a gradual process, but even small amounts of some Pfas are unsafe to consume. And though we don’t entirely know how bad microplastics are for our health, their growing prevalence everywhere ( even the soil ) is causing concern.

This past year we have tested plastic-free cutting boards, non-toxic pans, food storage containers and other kitchen tools to help you make well-informed decisions. Items free of Pfas and microplastics are investments, so we like to spotlight good deals when we find them. This week, we’re sharing two non-toxic cookware discounts worth a look. Both ranked highly in our testing.
After testing 13 non-toxic pans, Our Place’s Titanium Always Pan Pro emerged as our “best overall” winner.

“It heated up quickly, eggs slid off the pan smoothly, and proteins got an even sear despite the micro-dot ridges on the pan’s surface (that help with the non-stick effect),” write the scientists at Drexel’s Food Lab.

articles.title: I have noticed a pattern with product ratings that could lead to biased reviews. Is it legal?
articles.summary: The practice you’ve noticed is colloquially known as ‘review gating’, writes consumer affairs and policy professional Kat George. And no, it isn’t legal. I have noticed that when I get an email inviting me to review a product or service I have purchased online or physically, if I select a high…
body: Kat says: Screening reviews and sorting feedback based on a consumer’s initial sentiment is known colloquially online as “review gating”. It’s a dark pattern that is common enough that Google has banned it outright. And while the Australian consumer law doesn’t name the practice explicitly, it is clearly prohibited under laws relating to business reviews and false and misleading practices.

In early 2026, Google made some pointed changes to its Maps User Generated Content policy. The new policy states that Google does not allow businesses to “discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers”. What you have described sounds like businesses doing both of those things.

Google also has real consequences for businesses that are found to be in breach of its policy, so your experience is worth reporting directly to Google. Penalties include removing reviews that breach the policy, placing restrictions and alerts on business profiles, limiting the business’s eligibility to receive new reviews and temporarily hiding historical reviews.

articles.title: A Trump proposal would punish single parents. Other wealthy countries have a different approach
articles.summary: Canada, the Netherlands and Sweden offer extra support to solo-parent households. In its latest pronatalist push, the Trump administration aims to shift funds away from them.
body: When news broke that the Trump administration planned to pay married couples to have one parent stay home with their kids, everyone from policy wonks to Redditors bemoaned what they saw as a new front in the mommy wars.

The proposal would shift funds that subsidize childcare for low-income working parents – the majority of them single parents who rely on childcare providers – to low-income married couples with one earner. Given that most single parents and stay-at-home parents are women, and both groups would be applying for the same limited funds, it seemed almost designed to pit moms against each other.

Details on the policy, initially reported by the New York Times, are scant. However, like many of other nominally pronatalist policy proposals the administration has entertained so far, it appears this one is less focused on addressing the deeper challenges that face parents and aspiring parents as celebrating a throwback family structure.

San Francisco diners became acquainted with powerhouse couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz through their championing of Eastern Mediterranean cuisine at Dalida. That restaurant told the story of Sayat’s upbringing and influences in Istanbul, Turkey, opening in 2023 inside a historic building within the lush environs of the Presidio and earning critical acclaim for the duo’s cooking.

In the years since, diners came to know Laura outside of Dalida. She completed an impressive run on Top Chef in 2024, where viewers saw her deftly plant one foot in Mediterranean food and another in Mexican cuisine, showcasing her skill in both fields throughout the season. With the 2026 debut of the Ozyilmazes’ restaurant Maria Isabel, the food feels like an even fuller expression of Laura’s heritage and personal history.

articles.title: 25 Pages of Veruschka, Photographed by Avedon for Vogue in 1967
articles.summary: Ahead of the Ron Howard–directed Richard Avedon documentary, we share a 1967 an editorial from the archive that’s worth jumping up and down about.
body: Editor’s Note: Richard Avedon is always in fashion. That’s because he was interested in who people—be they impossibly beautiful models, activists, or punks—were under the surface. Director Ron Howard has taken a similar approach to the late photographer and his work in the new documentary, Avedon, out November 11 on Netflix. The release coincides with “ Richard Avedon: Hollywood,” an exhibition at the Gagosian gallery in Beverly Hills.

Avedon followed Diana Vreeland from Harper’s Bazaar to Vogue in 1966 and he stayed for 23 years. This 25-page editorial from 1967 features Veruschka, the model whom Avedon described as “the most beautiful woman in the world,” a woman whose beauty “demands something and you must extend yourself to meet the challenge or know that a kind of splendor is lost to you forever.” Nothing is lost in these images capturing Veruschka in movement; indeed, they document the symbiosis between artist and subject.
“Vogue’ s Eye View: Fashion for Eveyone–American Dresses Have It,” photographed by Richard Avedon, originally appeared in the March 1,1967 issue of the magazine.

articles.title: This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk
articles.summary: If you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws…
body: Whether you use a Mac or a PC, you probably browse the web with Chrome, or a Chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

As reported by The Hacker News, Google released a new update for Chrome on Monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

articles.title: Forget Blue Jeans, This Fall Is All About Coffee-Colored Denim
articles.summary: Brown jeans possess the same the versatility of black denim, but with a softer, more luxurious feel—here’s how to style it for fall, the street style way.
body: Blue denim might be fashion’s most enduring wardrobe staple, but this fall, I’m developing a taste for something a little richer. Enter a sophisticated palette of espresso, mocha and chocolate-brown jeans, which offer all the versatility of black denim, but with a softer, more luxurious feel. The street style set have already got the memo, of course, pairing their brown jeans –mostly of the wide-legged variety–with Penny Lane coats and oversized bombers. Below, discover how to wear autumn’s most appetizing denim trend.

Back in the early Noughties, we loved a fashion rule. Black and green should never be seen. A statement belt was essential for nipping in the waist. Black and brown make a frown. Thankfully, in 2026, we’re no longer beholden to the style diktats of yore. In fact, pairing coffee-coloured jeans with a black jacket is a failsafe way to ease into the trend.

Why stop at one coffee-colored piece when you could have the whole wardrobe? Once you’ve developed a taste for brown denim, it’s only a matter of time before the shade makes its way into the rest of your outfits. Break things up with a touch of grey, or go all in on head-to-toe tones.
